  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study reports quantitative measures of agreement between animal toxicology data and human clinical observations, specifically sensitivity (48%) and positive predictive value (43%), and negative predictive value (86%). It analyzes a database of molecules and their translation from nonclinical to clinical trials.",
  "arm": "toxicology",
  "arm_evidence": "The study analyzed animal toxicology data coupled with clinical observations from phase I human studies to determine how safety assessments in animal models translate to First-In-Human clinical risk.",

  "model_type": "regulatory-dataset",
  "model_evidence": "An industry-wide nonclinical to clinical translational database was created to determine how safety assessments in animal models translate to First-In-Human clinical risk.",
  "species": [
    "rat",
    "dog",
    "non-human-primate"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The nonhuman primate had the strongest performance in predicting adverse effects... The beagle dog had the strongest performance in predicting an absence of clinical adverse effects.",

  "endpoint_evidence": "Sensitivity was 48% with a 43% positive predictive value (PPV). Specificity was 84% with an 86% negative predictive value (NPV)."
